purpose: Matured, post-backfill re-take of docs/de-villa-cluster-baseline-2026-09-01.json. That snapshot's absolute numbers are understated by roughly an order of magnitude -- captured before SearchMetric's one-time 90-day backfill (see that file's own ingestCaveat). Comparing matured data against the unrevised baseline would read as growth that did not happen. This file is the comparable 'after' point, using the SAME canonicalization-pooled methodology as the original (urlCanonical.ts's buildCanonicalMap/canonicalize, folding each page's bare-English-prefix GSC duplicate into its /de/ canonical -- confirmed live this time by asking canonicalize() itself which (locale,page) pairs pool into each target, not assumed from memory).
caveat: Even matured GSC data keeps revising for roughly a month after each date, and ordinary drift is real on this cluster independent of any site change. These are ALL-TIME cumulative sums, same convention as the original -- not a rolling window -- so the comparison is more direct than the off-plan re-take's (which uses a 28-day window). A first pass at this re-take, done WITHOUT the canonicalization pooling, showed impressions apparently dropping 20-25% across all three pages despite MORE days of SearchMetric coverage than the original had -- which would have been a real, concerning finding. It was a methodology bug, not a real drop: the un-pooled pull was missing each page's bare-English-prefix duplicate series (e.g. en::/luxusvillen-in-zypern, which alone carries more impressions than the /de/ page), which the original snapshot's own methodology explicitly included. With pooling applied correctly, all three pages show growth, consistent with a matured backfill. Flagging this mistake here rather than silently discarding it, since the same trap is waiting for anyone re-pulling any canonicalized page's totals by hand.
